$comment: OBJECTS THE POSTGRESQL CAPABILITY AUTHORITY NAMES. Declared HERE, in the backend, and not in field-ops-app-vite/src/access/policyObjectRegistry.js, because a frontend catalog may not author the canonical Object <- action mapping (Owner ruling). Each exists because a row in eos_policy.capabilities points at it: migration 1761350400000 makes object_key NOT NULL, so a capability cannot name an Object the catalog does not define. None carries a field; they are security subjects, not data shapes.

objects.label: Principal
objects.description: The security actor: the authenticated identity that holds Security Roles and, through them, capabilities. NEVER the Employee -- an Employee is a workforce record and may exist with no Principal at all. Linked by eos_policy.employee_principal_links.

objects.label: Cycle Count
objects.description: A counting sheet over stock at a location, from creation through submit, reconcile and close. Governed by eos_ops.cycle_count_sheets.

objects.label: Data Import
objects.description: An administrative import batch that turns an approved preview into governed EOS records. NONPRODUCTION-ONLY tooling; its retirement is tracked separately and this registration does not endorse a production path.

objects.label: Workflow
objects.description: A governed workflow and its versions, steps, actions and Role bindings. Steps, actions and bindings are version-scoped sub-entities, not Objects of their own.

objects.label: Report Definition
objects.description: A saved report definition: what it selects and how it is shaped. Registered by migration 1762300800000 as Reporting Slice 1, mirroring workflowDefinition -- a security subject with no data shape of its own. It carries NO field dimension: eos_policy.capabilities has object_key NOT NULL, UNIQUE (object_key, action_key) and no field column, so a field-level report id cannot be a capability row of this Object. Firebase exit B4 (DECISIONS #B4, migration 1764640000000) registers the report object and field reads under the separate `report` Object, and the saved-definition mutations here.

objects.label: Workflow Instance
objects.description: One running workflow over one business record, pinned to the version it began under. Registered as a governed Object; it has NO capability yet, because execution security must be designed together with target-Object enforcement rather than back-filled to populate a matrix.

objects.label: Inbound Work Request
objects.description: A received request for service work (email intake) under review: read, and dispositioned by Accept (an EOS Work Order is created), Attach (associated with an existing Work Order) or Decline. Governed by eos_ops.inbound_work_requests (migration 1764340000000). A security subject; the business record is the intake.

objects.label: Inbound Mailbox
objects.description: The intake configuration Inbound Work is received through: the mailboxes EOS knows and their routing rules (eos_ops.inbound_mailboxes, eos_ops.inbound_routing_rules; migration 1764340000000). Managed by inboundWork.intake.manage. Provider/OAuth custody is not part of this Object.

objects.label: Finance Configuration
objects.description: Administrative Finance configuration (DECISIONS #203 / #204): each operating company's provider-neutral accounting destination and company / counterparty payment terms (net days, governing future obligations). Managed by finance.configuration.manage. No financial transaction, settlement, delivery, credential or business approval is part of this Object.

objects.label: System Configuration
objects.description: Governed company / system settings (Owner ruling #204): each operating company's business time zone and default language, by one settings registry. Managed by admin.systemConfiguration.manage (system administration). Confers no business approval.

objects.label: Sales Discount Authority
objects.description: Employee Sales Authority (Owner ruling #204): each Sales user's maximum customer discount percentage, governing only the customer-facing transaction discount. Managed by sales.discountAuthority.manage. Never internal pricing, cost, trade-in value or resale price.

objects.label: Settlement
objects.description: Operational settlement evidence (DECISIONS #206): a customer payment, provider funding receipt, vendor payment or intercompany payment / receipt for one operating company and one counterparty, its application to obligations, its correction and its reconciliation evidence. Never a bank fact; EOS is not the GL.

objects.label: Rental Agreement
objects.description: A Rental Agreement (DECISIONS #207): Taylor-owned equipment rented to a customer site under versioned agreed terms (rate, billing frequency, expected end, governed delivery / install charges), and the explicit billing eligibility of its whole periods and one-time charges. Never a sale, never financing; ownership never moves.

objects.label: Rental Equipment
objects.description: The rental fleet (DECISIONS #207): Taylor-owned serialized units designated for rental, their availability (available / reserved / on rent / service hold / return pending / inspection / unavailable), assignment to agreements, return into Taylor custody and inspection.

objects.label: Financial Policy
objects.description: An operating company's governed accounting-policy profile (DECISIONS #232, continuing the CERT-FIN-02 ruling of 2026-09-03): inventory cost method, serialized cost method, COGS recognition point and freight / landed-cost treatment, held as versions -- DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED or REJECTED, ACTIVE (locked), SUPERSEDED. Taylor and Ventana keep independent policies. Prepared by Finance, approved and activated by the Owner or the Administrator; a preparer never approves their own submission.

objects.label: Inventory Return
objects.description: A returned item taken in (DECISIONS #242, Firebase exit F7a): the operating company receiving it, an optional receiving warehouse, its source, part, quantity or serials, observed condition and reason, recorded AWAITING_DISPOSITION. Intake only -- no ledger movement, never restored to sellable stock (#118). Its one capability, inventory.returns.intake, is a business action, so no CRED verb is derived from it.

objects.label: CRM Activity
objects.description: An interaction logged on a customer Account (DECISIONS #243, Firebase exit F7b): a call, meeting, sales note, relationship touch or general note, when it happened and who recorded it, with optional links to the Account's own Contact, Opportunity or Sales Order. Reading it also requires reading the Account. No CRED verb is derived here: its two capabilities are projected under this Object by Administration.

objects.label: Report
objects.description: The data a report may read (Firebase exit B4, DECISIONS #B4): one object-level read per reportable record type (Customer, Contact, Location, Equipment) and one read per field group, registered under the Firebase catalog's own ids report.<object>.read and report.<object>.field.<group>.read. A security subject, not a data shape: it carries no field of its own and no CRED verb is derived, because a run re-decides the object, every field and the caller's operating companies.

objects.label: Performance Goal
objects.description: A governed performance goal: a versioned, effective-dated, approved TARGET (never an actual), read by scope (Firebase exit B4, DECISIONS #B4). Its one capability is performance.goal.read; the Firebase authoring verbs (create, approve, supersede, retire) have no EOS consumer yet and are not registered. A security subject with no field and no CRED verb.
